context: I have a £20,000 inheritance to invest. My instinct is to
completion_high: put most of it into equities for long-run growth, accepting the short-term swings.
completion_low: keep most of it in a high-yield savings account where the principal is safe.
notes: Equity vs cash — core DOSPERT-Financial dimension

context: Offered the chance to invest in a friend's well-thought-through but unproven business, I would
completion_high: commit a meaningful slice of my discretionary capital.
completion_low: decline politely; early-stage private investments are too risky for me.

context: When deciding between two pension allocations, one with 80% equity and one with 40% equity, I
completion_high: go with 80% equity for the long horizon.
completion_low: go with 40% equity for the smoother ride.

context: Asked whether to take a 30-year fixed mortgage or a 5-year tracker, I
completion_high: take the tracker to capture rate falls; I can refinance if rates spike.
completion_low: take the 30-year fixed for predictability.

context: Offered an asymmetric trade — pay £2,000 for a 25% chance at £20,000 — I
completion_high: take it; the expected value justifies the variance.
completion_low: decline; losing £2,000 outright is too likely.

context: When a friend asks me whether to invest a windfall in a single high-conviction stock, I'd say
completion_high: if the conviction is real and the position size is right, go.
completion_low: diversify; concentrating in one name is gambling.

context: Approached about a fund returning 12% historical with above-average drawdowns, I would
completion_high: allocate to it as a satellite to a core index position.
completion_low: stick with the boring low-fee index fund.

context: When my brokerage offers 2× margin on an index ETF I want to hold for years, I
completion_high: use modest leverage if I can stomach the variance.
completion_low: stay unleveraged; margin is how people lose money.

context: Asked whether to buy a rental property with 80% loan-to-value, I
completion_high: do it if the deal pencils — leverage is the point of property.
completion_low: wait until I can put 50% down; I don't want to be over-extended.

context: Considering whether to keep £100,000 in cash or deploy it into the market today, I
completion_high: deploy it — time in the market beats timing the market.
completion_low: keep it in cash and average in over 12 months.

context: Offered the chance to put 5% of my net worth into a friend's seed-stage startup, I
completion_high: take it; it's exactly the size of bet that doesn't matter if it goes to zero.
completion_low: decline; even 5% feels like real money.

context: When my employer offers a stock-grant top-up that increases my exposure to one company, I
completion_high: take the grant; I already trust the company enough to work there.
completion_low: ask for cash equivalent; concentrating my income and equity in one place is dangerous.

context: Asked to lend a friend £5,000 with their handshake on repayment, I
completion_high: lend it; I trust them and can absorb the loss if it doesn't come back.
completion_low: decline; mixing money and friendship is a bad idea.

context: When a counterparty wants to settle a deal in equity rather than cash, I
completion_high: consider the equity if I believe in the company.
completion_low: insist on cash; equity that can't be sold is worth less than the headline.

context: Offered the choice between a guaranteed £5,000 bonus or a 50% chance at £15,000, I
completion_high: take the gamble; expected value is higher.
completion_low: take the guaranteed amount.
notes: Classic risk-aversion paradigm. Note: pure-chance gamble — should covary with dospert_gambling more than dospert_investing

context: Considering whether to put 20% of my retirement funds into emerging-market equities, I
completion_high: do it; the expected long-run premium is worth the volatility.
completion_low: stick with developed markets; emerging-market drawdowns are punishing.

context: When my financial adviser suggests a 60/40 stock/bond portfolio at age 35, I
completion_high: ask for 90/10; I have decades to absorb volatility.
completion_low: agree; 60/40 is the standard for a reason.

context: Faced with a 10-year zero-coupon bond yielding 5%, I'd
completion_high: consider it for the duration play; I can hold to maturity.
completion_low: stick with shorter duration; locking in 10 years feels exposed.

context: Offered to early-cash a vested stock option grant or hold to expiry, I
completion_high: hold and let the upside play out.
completion_low: exercise and lock in the value I have.

context: When evaluating whether to refinance my mortgage to take cash out for an investment, I
completion_high: do it if the spread between mortgage rate and expected return is big enough.
completion_low: leave the equity in the home; debt for investment is too risky.

context: If a colleague asks whether they should buy a single tech stock with their savings, I'd say
completion_high: if the conviction holds and the stake isn't your whole net worth, go for it.
completion_low: no — buy a diversified fund; single names are gambling.

context: When my income jumps and I have £10,000 extra at year end, I
completion_high: deploy it into the market straight away.
completion_low: park it in cash for a few months and decide later.

context: Considering whether to take a personal loan at 7% to buy index funds returning 9% historically, I
completion_high: do it; the carry is positive and I'm comfortable with the variance.
completion_low: pay off existing debt instead; borrowing to invest is reckless.

context: Faced with a six-month-emergency-fund decision, I
completion_high: keep three months and invest the rest; emergencies are rarer than the cost of cash drag.
completion_low: keep the full six months; you can't rewind a layoff.

context: Offered a private credit fund yielding 9% with 3-year lockup, I'd
completion_high: consider it for the yield; I don't need the liquidity for that money.
completion_low: skip it; locking up capital for 3 years is dangerous.

context: Asked whether to buy a quality apartment as my first investment property, I
completion_high: do it if the cash flow holds at moderate vacancy.
completion_low: rent and invest the difference; property is illiquid and concentrated.

context: When my bank offers a structured product 'capital protected, equity-linked', I
completion_high: skip it; the structure shaves return for protection I don't need.
completion_low: consider it; principal protection is worth giving up some upside.
notes: Inverted item — high-DOSPERT prefers underlying equity, low prefers principal protection

context: Considering whether to accept a job with 30% lower base + meaningful equity at a startup, I
completion_high: take it; the equity upside dominates the salary cut.
completion_low: stay where I am; equity is a lottery ticket on top of a real wage.

context: Offered the choice between a 4% government bond and an 8% high-yield corporate bond, I'd
completion_high: take the corporate; the spread compensates for the credit risk.
completion_low: take the government; the haircut isn't worth the default risk.

context: Faced with a 50% drawdown in my portfolio, I would
completion_high: buy more — the underlying didn't change, the price did.
completion_low: rotate to safer assets to stop the bleeding.
notes: Drawdown response — drives realised vs unrealised behaviour

context: When considering whether to put 30% of my net worth into a single asset class, I
completion_high: do it if I have the highest conviction in that class.
completion_low: spread it; concentration is the enemy.

context: If a tax-advantaged investment option carries higher fees and lower expected return, I
completion_high: skip it; tax savings rarely compensate for fee drag.
completion_low: take it; the tax certainty is worth the cost.
notes: Tax-vs-return optimisation. Inverted-leaning: the high-risk-taker prefers raw return

context: When weighing whether to keep an underperforming investment or sell, I
completion_high: sell if the thesis broke; sunk cost is irrelevant.
completion_low: hold and wait for it to recover so I'm not selling at a loss.
notes: Loss aversion — high DOSPERT-Financial overrides loss aversion

context: Offered to put 2% of my net worth into crypto, I
completion_high: do it as a small high-conviction satellite.
completion_low: skip it; speculative assets aren't real investments.

context: Considering an angel investment in a sector I understand deeply, I'd
completion_high: lean in if the founders are strong; my edge here is real.
completion_low: stick with passive index investing; the variance isn't worth it.
notes: Edge-gated investing — central to Rick's profile

context: When my business has £200,000 in surplus cash and steady demand, I
completion_high: deploy it into growth — marketing, hiring, capacity.
completion_low: hold it as a runway buffer.

context: Offered to take on a £100,000 SBA loan for business expansion, I
completion_high: take it if the unit economics support the debt.
completion_low: decline; the personal guarantee is too exposed.

context: If a long-term annuity locks in 4% real return for life, I
completion_high: skip it; equities will beat it over my horizon.
completion_low: take it; locking in real return removes the worst tail.

context: Considering whether to delay a planned house purchase to keep capital liquid for investing, I'd
completion_high: delay; productive capital beats home equity for a few more years.
completion_low: buy; lock in the housing decision and stop renting.

context: Faced with a high-yield short-term bond with B-rated issuer, I
completion_high: take a small position; the yield justifies the credit risk at this size.
completion_low: skip; I don't reach for yield in fixed income.

context: When my portfolio has had a 30% gain in 12 months, I
completion_high: rebalance back to target weights but stay invested.
completion_low: take some off the table; gains aren't real until they're realised.

context: Asked whether to put a year's worth of pension contributions into the market in January or spread across the year, I
completion_high: front-load in January.
completion_low: spread monthly; less regret if January is the top.

context: When considering whether to sell an asset that has appreciated and incur capital gains tax, I
completion_high: sell if the next opportunity is better; tax shouldn't trap capital.
completion_low: hold; the deferred tax is worth the suboptimal allocation.

context: If offered a hedge-fund seat with 2-and-20 fees and a strong track record, I
completion_high: take it; the after-fee alpha is the question.
completion_low: skip; high fees almost always erase advertised alpha.
notes: High-fee active product. Note: high DOSPERT here may also reflect high openness; check covariance

context: When my closest friends are all buying property and I'm renting, I
completion_high: stay invested in liquid assets; renting and investing is a real strategy.
completion_low: buy; everyone owning a home isn't a coincidence.

context: Considering whether to use a tax-loss harvest in a falling market, I
completion_high: do it; banking the loss is a free option.
completion_low: skip; the wash-sale rules and complexity aren't worth it.

context: If my investment thesis turns out wrong after six months, I
completion_high: exit the position and redeploy.
completion_low: hold for now; markets are noisy and I might still be right.
notes: Thesis-discipline. Adjacent to dospert_investing — willingness to act on falsification

context: When picking between a 15-year mortgage at 5% and a 30-year at 5.5%, I
completion_high: take the 30-year and invest the savings.
completion_low: take the 15-year for the lower total interest.

context: Faced with a structured deal that pays out only if a specific event occurs, I
completion_high: size it as a small bet and take the asymmetric upside.
completion_low: skip; bet-the-event products are gambling.

context: When the market is volatile and the news cycle is bearish, my behaviour is to
completion_high: stay the course or buy more.
completion_low: raise cash until things calm down.
